title: Metric sparsity & alert threshold prototypes (investigation & experiments)
content:
Purpose: capture a lightweight investigative thread and experimental runbook for recurring short-lived missing metrics and noisy SLO-burn alerts. Goal is to prototype alert rule changes + lightweight synthetic heartbeats and validate rollout plan to reduce pager noise without hiding real regressions.

Summary of problem (observed pattern):
- Over the last 3 weeks we have multiple pages for SLO burn on model-inference P99 latency and downstream token throughput alerts. Many pages are short (2-10 minutes) then self-heal.
- On-call investigation repeatedly shows: Prometheus returns empty/low-sample histograms for route-specific metrics (route_latency_seconds_bucket, tokens_served_total) for short windows.
- Alerts are firing because current rules treat any recent missing datapoint as a breach (absent_over_time) and SLO burn alert uses a narrow window (5m) and derivative of low-count counters => sensitive to scrape jitter.

Recent timeline (high level):
- 2025-03-02 04:12 UTC: first large flurry; 14 pages in 3 hours, 70% auto-resolved within 8 minutes.
- 2025-03-18 11:37 UTC: replicated with increased frequency after canary config change to autoscaler (see RINF-2345).
- 2025-03-28 09:04 UTC: oncall notes indicate Prometheus target timeouts spiked during same window.

Key signals & queries used during troubleshooting (examples):
- Check raw cardinality and scrape success: up{job="model-inference"} and scrape_duration_seconds{job="prometheus"}
- Detect sparse counters: count_over_time(model_inference_tokens_served_total[10m]) < 3
- Absent detector we use today: absent_over_time(route_latency_seconds_count{route=~".*"}[5m]) > 0
- Alternative probe to measure sparsity: avg_over_time(rate(model_inference_tokens_served_total[5m])[10m:1m])

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Scrape interference: high cardinality + transient scale events cause Prometheus to timeout or drop series, creating apparent "missing" metrics. Evidence: concurrent scrape_duration_seconds spikes and up counts dipping.
2) Instrumentation flush semantics: service process restarts (graceful or OOM) lead to histogram buckets resetting and short-lived empty counts.
3) Alert rule fragility: derivative-based or absent-based alerts on small-count series lead to high sensitivity to jitter.
4) Edge-case exporter bug: exporter for some routes sometimes stalls under CPU pressure and fails to update gauges for a few seconds.

Low-effort experiments to test hypotheses (quick, reversible):
- E1: Add a synthetic heartbeat metric from the service with very low cardinality: model_inference_heartbeat{instance,region}. Increment every 60s. Use this as a signal for "service alive" and gate SLO-burn alerts: only evaluate SLO alert when heartbeat present for 2/3 of window.
- E2: Increase scrape timeout for model-inference job from 10s to 20s in Prometheus for a 24h canary. Rationale: if scraping was timing out we want to see reduction in absent series.
- E3: Replace absent_over_time(...) conditions with a combination of count_over_time(...) and max_over_time(...): require a minimum sample count before triggering. Prototype rule below.
- E4: Add a 1-minute smoothing window for derivative-based rules (use increase() instead of rate() on very small counters).

Prototype alert rules (draft expressions):
- Alert: RouteMetricSparsityHigh
  Expr: count_over_time(route_latency_seconds_count{env="prod"}[10m]) < 5 and 
        absent_over_time(model_inference_heartbeat{env="prod"}[10m]) == 0
  For: 10m
  Note: require both low sample count and heartbeat present (i.e., service alive but sparse metrics).

- Alert: SLOBurnCandidate (smoothed)
  Expr: (sum by(route)(increase(route_request_latency_bucket{le=+Inf}[30m])) / sum by(route)(increase(route_request_total[30m]))) > 0.02
  For: 30m
  Note: move to 30m evaluation to reduce sensitivity to short blips.

Runbook (oncall) - quick triage steps:
1) Check heartbeat: promql 'model_inference_heartbeat{env="prod"}' over 30m. If heartbeat absent for >5m, escalate to infra (possible process down or network partition).
2) Check Prometheus scrape targets: promtool query 'up{job="model-inference"}' and 'scrape_duration_seconds{job="prometheus",instance=~"prom-*"}'
3) If up shows intermittent target drops, check network egress/errors on the source host (kubectl logs for node/proxy, check kubelet events).
4) If heartbeat present but route metrics sparse: run 'count_over_time(route_latency_seconds_count{route="/v1/generate"}[15m])' and inspect exporter logs for the service instance(s) with highest cardinality.
5) If histogram buckets reset: correlate with process restarts (kubectl get pods --sort-by=.status.startTime and check recent restarts).
6) Temporary mitigations: apply an alert mute for the noisy route for 1 hour with documented reason if noise is confirmed and incident impact low. File postmortem if mute > 3 hours.
7) Escalation: if SLO burn continues > 1hr and user-visible errors increase, page product-sre/infra and open RINF ticket.

Risk analysis and tradeoffs:
- Increasing evaluation windows reduces false positives but increases mean time to detection for real regressions. We propose rolling changes: widen windows for noisy, low-cardinality per-route alerts, keep tight SLAs for top-level customer-facing metrics.
- Adding heartbeat metric reduces false positives but can mask real outages if heartbeat itself fails; keep heartbeat simple and low-cardinality and monitor its own health.

Canary & rollout plan:
- Day 0: deploy E1 heartbeat to 10% of instances in us-west region for 48h. Monitor pager counts and absent_over_time signals.
- Day 2: if heartbeat reduces noise by >50% without masking real alerts, roll heartbeat to all prod and update alert gating.
- Day 3: apply rule changes (increase windows, add sample-count thresholds) in Prometheus in dry-run mode (alertmanager silence simulation) and monitor.

Open tasks and owners: (assignments)
- Nora: implement heartbeat probe in model-inference service and open PR (github PR link in linked_artifacts). (RINF-2345)
- Ethan: deploy Prometheus scrape timeout change to staging and run synthetic scraping load test. (RINF-2390)
- Priya: prototype updated alert rules in dev Prometheus and simulate noisy patterns. (RINF-2412)
- Maya: create dashboard tile for count_over_time(route_latency_seconds_count[30m]) and hook to SLO on-call view. (RINF-2421)

Unresolved questions / notes to revisit:
- How to handle cardinality explosion if we add synthetic heartbeat with labels per route? Recommendation: only include instance+region labels (no route label).
- Should we maintain a separate "health" Prometheus job with a longer scrape timeout for low-cardinality health metrics? Pros/cons need cost analysis.
- Confirm exporter bug theory: need trace-level logs from exporter under CPU pressure windows.

Retrospective metrics to evaluate success:
- Pager count reduction for SLO-burn/absent alerts (target: 60% reduction in noisy pages over 30 days).
- Mean time to detection for real regressions (ensure < baseline*1.25).
- Number of false-mute incidents (goal: 0).

References & context:
- Related oncall notes: see slack thread in linked_artifacts.
- Prior similar effort: small scrape-timeout increase in 2024 reduced similar noise on billing-service (internal note).

Notes to self: keep rule changes reversible, prefer gradual rollout and strong telemetry around muted alerts. If any change causes missed customer-facing SLO degradations we revert immediately and do a postmortem.

End of scratchpad. Next sync: weekly SRE observability sync on Fridays to review canary metrics and decide on broader rollout.
